importance_ranking.reason: Greenhouse Type, Area Range, and Turnkey Scope are primary shortlisting gates — a buyer needing a 2,000 sq mt NHB-compliant NVPH cannot evaluate a listing that does not specify these. Without matching specs, no further engagement occurs.

Per sq mt rate varies substantially across greenhouse types (NVPH vs Fan & Pad vs Polycarbonate) and project scale. Indian agri-buyers compare per-sq-mt rates against NHB cost norms as a primary budget check once structure type is confirmed.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some contractors quote lump-sum per project for small farms — this creates price comparison confusion. Per sq mt is the NHB/NHM standard and must be shown alongside price to enable meaningful comparison.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing the unit. Per sq mt vs per project is a real market ambiguity; NHB cost norms are defined per sq mt and buyers use this unit as their reference benchmark.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in Indian greenhouse construction — market is fragmented across regional contractors and fabricators; buyers search by spec, area coverage, and NHB empanelment status, not contractor brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: NHB empanelment status, state service coverage, past project track record, and execution capability are evaluated during vendor selection — particularly for large capital projects where post-sale service and warranty matter.

Completed project photos help buyers assess build quality, structural finish, and structural type — functioning as a trust and quality signal. However, spec text already captures structure type, so image is a qualifier rather than a primary shortlisting gate for this service category.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the product class — NVPH, Fan & Pad, Shade Net, and Polycarbonate are non-interchangeable structure types with large per-sq-mt cost differences driven by material and system complexity.

Determines project scale and total contract value; contractors specialise in scale tiers and buyers have fixed land parcels, making this a non-substitutable shortlisting filter with significant cost implications.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Agent 3 market_context explicitly identifies ventilation system as a key buyer decision driver — NVPH structures can have different passive ventilation configurations, and Fan & Pad systems are a distinct premium tier; sellers need this to confirm they supply the required climate control approach.

NHB/NHM subsidy compliance is a primary buyer decision driver per Agent 3 market_context — NHB-compliant construction requires specific material standards (B-Class GI pipe, 200-micron UV film) and documentation support that not all contractors provide.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Defines the structural form the buyer requires — sellers need this to confirm they construct that type and to provide an accurate per-sq-mt quote.

Tells sellers whether irrigation integration is in scope and what type — drip vs hydroponics vs aeroponics differ substantially in complexity and cost, materially affecting the seller's ability to respond accurately.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers cannot generate a meaningful quote without knowing the project area — per-sq-mt pricing and total contract value are entirely dependent on covered area, and NHB/NHM subsidy tier eligibility is defined by area thresholds.

Sellers need to know if the project must meet NHB or NHM compliance standards — subsidised projects require specific material grades, documentation support, and empanelment status that not all contractors possess.
